subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The True Cost to Victims
description: A quick, practical guide to The True Cost to Victims.

hook.text: The average identity theft victim spends over 200 hours and $1,300 repairing the damage.

buildup.text: Beyond money, victims report anxiety, depression, and difficulty trusting people.

discovery.text: Some victims are denied jobs, loans, or housing because of fraudulent records in their name.

twist.text: Even after resolution, stolen data remains on the dark web — meaning the risk never fully ends.

climax.text: Identity theft is not a one-time event. It's an ongoing threat that can resurface years later.

punchline.text: The theft takes seconds. The cleanup takes years.

quiz.question: Why doesn't the risk end after resolving identity theft?
options: Stolen data remains on the dark web indefinitely
